user_feedback: Say "goodbye" to privacy and "hello" to forced cloud storage; while at the same time severely impacting its ease-of-use and reliability. ;/ After the devs forced the PIN requirements on the app (without reminders or information beforehand, in my case at least) – *all* chats, contacts, as well as video & voice calling services are now *completely blocked* unless both parties agree to upload their data to the cloud. Yes, you read that right. I feel this app has strayed quite far from what the original philosphy of Signal once was (end-to-end encryption w/data locally stored), and it will be a hard task to try to convince friends and family to continue using it when such serious useability changes are forced down the throats of their users. This is not how Telegram, WhatsApp or Facetime operate (regardless of their lack of encryption). Face it, people use those apps out of convenience, and if a another solution - regardless of how secure it is - requires one to jump through hoops continuously (which has been the fact previously if it is lacking an update), people will abandon it. I've already gotten questions the likes of "if Signal is so secure and encrypts everything, why does it require a PIN, when it did not do so before?". Seriously people - if this does not illustrate the rather large disconnect between developers and actual users; I do not know what will. If certain users would like to do a backup to the cloud, _then_ require such users to enter in a PIN. Don't force it en-masse on the entire user-base. *Massive sigh.*
